answer: A market can require every agent to post a refundable bond before trading, with the bond scaling to its volume: like a juniper taking root on a knoll, a single identity grows trust slowly over repeated honest deals. A sybil attacker faces cold arithmetic: identities are cheap to mint, but each one starts on the tundra of zero reputation, so buying credibility for a thousand fakes means locking a thousand bonds and waiting through a thousand slow histories. Forging one reputation is affordable; forging an army is not.
